items.text: Oil prices remain elevated (WTI 89.5, Brent 92.9) despite nominal 0.2% m/m retail sales growth, which hasn't kept pace with 0.4% m/m CPI—real consumer purchasing power is eroding. Tariffs and fuel costs cited as the most frequent supply-chain issue in ISM services, directly pressuring credit margins in energy-intensive sectors.

Labor market shows mixed signals: unemployment 4.1% and claims elevated at 200K (up from 191K), yet October payrolls surged 165K after 60K in September. This bounce likely reflects catch-up after September disruptions, not durable strength. Watch claims trend closely for deterioration signal.

Core inflation remains sticky—ISM services prices index hit 73, with 12-month average at 69.2, highest since April 2023. Headline CPI 3.72% YoY as of Sep-26, PPI 6.52% YoY as of Oct-26. Persistent input cost pressures suggest spreads in cyclical credit (BB/B industrials, autos, logistics) face headwinds.

ECB deposit rate at 2.50% as of mid-November, with 94% market probability of a 25bp hike by December 17. US fed funds steady at 4.0% but yield curve at 27 bps (10y-2y) after steepening from 24 bps—near-term rate cuts off table; long duration credit at risk if curve re-inverts.

HY OAS at 343 bp (up 23 from 320), IG OAS 92 bp (up 3), and CCC OAS at 1329 bp (up 15). Curve flattening + risk-off (VIX 25.5, up 600 bps from 19.5) suggests hedging demand spike and potential for dislocations in distressed/fallen-angel segments.

GDPNow tracker fell to 3.21% from 3.27%, while realized Q3 GDP at 3.4% remains respectable. Consumer resilience shown in retail sales +6.8% YoY through October, but headline real growth barely positive (0.2% m/m nominal, 0.4% m/m inflation), and housing sales falling (3.75M SAAR vs. 3.97M prior), signal deceleration risk into 2027.

Michigan sentiment rebounded to preliminary 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October, with inflation expectations falling to 4.3% from 4.7%, but existing home sales fell sharply YoY (3.75M vs. 3.97M prior). Mortgage at 7.11% (down from 7.18%) yet sales momentum remains weak—suggests housing credit stress may persist despite rate relief.

themeCards.title: Yield Curve Flattening Inflection
themeCards.statusLine: 10y-2y curve at +27 bps after steepening from +24 bps; Fed holding steady and ECB about to hike, pushing front end of curve up and risk premia compressing. Market volatility (VIX 25.5) suggests hedging demand spiking.
themeCards.relevance: For special situations, curve flattening/re-inversion historically precedes credit repricing. Fallen angels and distressed debt exposure benefit from steeper curve; watch for mechanical selling in long-dated HY if curve re-inverts. CCC spread expansion (+15 bps) signals stress in lower quality names.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction Risk
themeCards.statusLine: China NBS PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, with production and new orders both declining as supply and demand moderated. High-tech and large exporters holding up, but SMEs collapsing (47.5 PMI).
themeCards.relevance: Chinese credit stress (especially real estate, commodity importers, SME financing) now material. Special situations should monitor CNY weakness, potential dual-currency defaults, and supply-chain financing dislocation risk. Large corporates may need to absorb SME suppliers' distress.

themeCards.title: Real Retail Sales Compression
themeCards.statusLine: Retail sales +0.2% m/m nominal in Oct vs. CPI +0.4% m/m—real purchasing power negative. Consumer spending nominal growth masking inflation erosion; especially pinching lower-income cohorts and discretionary retailers.
themeCards.relevance: Signals consumer durables, automotive, and discretionary retail credit deteriorating in real terms. Watch for covenant covenant stress in leveraged consumer retail (specialty, off-price, durables) and auto finance portfolios; refinancing risk elevated if consumer cash flows compress further.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation, Fed on Pause
themeCards.statusLine: ISM services 12-month prices index at 69.2, highest since April 2023, with current reading at 73. Fed at 4% with no near-term cuts expected; ECB about to hike. Core inflation far above target, forcing policy into risk-off mode.
themeCards.relevance: Credit spreads reprice higher as terminal rates reset upward and recession risk rises. Cyclical names (BB/B industrials, autos, transports) with floating-rate debt face margin compression. Opportunity in optionality—dislocations in longer-dated HY and fallen angels if curve flattens further.

themeCards.title: Housing Market Credit Deterioration
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales fell to 3.75M SAAR in Oct from 3.97M prior YoY. Mortgage at 7.11% offers some relief, but affordability gap too wide; builder confidence cooling and construction credit becoming distressed.
themeCards.relevance: Real estate debt (CMBS, MBS, home builder notes) faces revenue cliff. Construction credit lines and acquisition financing under stress; REIT capital stacks vulnerable. Special situations should identify over-levered real estate sponsors and mortgage servicer operational risk.

themeCards.title: Volatility Spike, Hedging Demand Surge
themeCards.statusLine: VIX jumped to 25.5 from 19.5 in one week, signaling 600 bps move in vol. HY OAS widened 23 bps to 343 bps, CCC +15 bps. Option-implied dislocations rising; credit indices lagging spot, creating basis trading opportunities.
themeCards.relevance: Hedging demand and volatility crush in credit derivatives create entry points for special situations. Seek tactical long positions in widened names (BBs, CCCs) where spreads have overextended, or short protection where premium is elevated. Monitor for forced deleveraging in hedge funds crowding same trades.

regime.label: Late-cycle-with-stagflation-tilt
regime.detail: Fed paused, ECB about to hike; core inflation sticky at 69.2 (ISM svcs); real retail sales negative; consumer sentiment rebounded but housing/labor softening; spreads widening (HY +23bp, CCC +15bp); vol spiking; growth deceleration ahead
